about: Where every rule lives (research/open-builder/HANDOFF.md section 4): each verify check and each rule line of the build brief has exactly one home. invariant: true of every game whatever its kind. part: belongs to one mechanic, world, loop, panel or engine (`part` says which). game: a promise this one game makes. nowhere: taste, an accident, or something the kit now prevents. tests/h-homes.test.mjs fails when a check or a brief line has no home, when a tag is stale, and when the brief passes its budget. Read and checked by tools/lib/homes.mjs (node research/gf-three/tools/lib/homes.mjs --lines).

1.name: manifests
1.rule: assets.json and multiplayer.json are valid, assets.json holds exactly the slots the game's declarations give, and the game is live multiplayer.
1.fix: Run node research/gf-three/tools/fix.mjs <game>: it puts back a slot the declarations give and assets.json lacks, and says so (slots.mjs <game> --write rebuilds the whole file). A slot nothing declares: declare it (a rules number in config/game.json → rules.params, a prop in config/world.json) or delete it. Keep multiplayer.json mode "live" as create wrote it.

2.name: kit copies unedited
2.rule: The kit copies in the game (gf/, audio/, vendor/) are byte for byte the kit's.
2.fix: Undo any edit under game/gf, game/audio or game/vendor (run create again without --force to refresh them). Put the game's own code in rules.js. An import of a three.js addon create did not vendor fails here too: use what vendor/ has.

3.name: boots to play with no console errors
3.rule: The game boots to play with no console errors, and the player moves on real keys.
3.fix: Open the game and read the console: fix the first error in rules.js (a syntax error or a throw in setup, roundStart or update stops the whole page). If the player cannot walk, check that nothing in rules.js freezes or re-places the local player every frame.

also.what: the walk test (W and D move the avatar): a game with no avatar has nothing to walk

when a part of the game owns player.control by its own manifest (a board with a cursor), the walk test reads the part's own sign of the player moving, their mark (snapshot().players[].mark from the part's presence(p)); a part that holds the body and reports no mark fails as a body that cannot walk does

4.name: slot coverage 100%
4.rule: Everything visible is a slot: every mesh on screen carries a slot id, in play and in every preview subject, and the game's own code builds nothing to draw.
4.fix: Do not build meshes in rules.js: no new geometry, mesh or sprite in the game's own code, whatever slot id it is given. Place a prop through config/world.json or a mechanic, show state through the kit part that draws it (a mechanic's own marker, ctx.vfx, ctx.ui and the nameplate), and read colours and numbers through ctx.assets and ctx.config. The detail names the untagged meshes and the lines that build one.
4.note: Second half since 2026-10-11 (tools/lib/improvised-check.mjs, the creator's question 19): a reading of the game's own scripts for constructed geometry. X1 built one spec nine times and four builds drew a cone in code with 100% coverage. A round game's flow only.

5.name: two-player live gate
5.rule: Two players over real WebRTC are in one game: each screen draws the other where they are, in their own look, and the shared state matches.
5.fix: Keep shared state on the host (if (ctx.host)), send events on edges and never every frame, use ctx.rng() instead of Math.random, and read a player's colour or model per player: ctx.assets.value(slotId, fallback, { player: p }).

also.what: the loadout leg (each player drawn in their own body and shot colour on the other screen)

a part that holds the body says where the player is (presence(p)): the kit's gate block reports the mark as the player's place, with mark: true, so the gate's 'movement shows on the other screen' is judged on what the friend sees move

6.name: a round reaches results and replays
6.rule: A round ends in results and Play again starts round 2, alone with bots and with two players.
6.fix: Let the kit end the round (the clock, or rules.check returning a result). Do not hold the phase in rules.js, and reset the game's own state in rules.roundStart so round 2 starts clean.

7.name: audio gate v5
7.rule: The round is heard through the gf-audio kit: the loudest sound is clearly audible while it sounds, sounds really start and reach the speakers, the game's own listed sounds are among them, and nothing is too loud, harsh, clipped or piled up.
7.fix: Play sounds only through ctx.audio with ids listed in assets.json → sounds → sounds, and make sure the round reaches them (a mechanic's sound param, a ctx.audio.play in the rules where the thing happens). A sound that is too quiet has too low a gainDb of its own. Do not play a sound every frame, and do not raise the bus levels to pass.

also.what: the solo round the gate listens to is cut to 25 s through round.seconds and what the flow's signs.short adds (a turn clock of 4 s, so pieces land inside the window); the targets and the kit's levels are the same for every flow

7.note: v5 (research/audio/qa-gate-v5.mjs, 2026-10-11) for a round game; a world and a forge game still run v4 in their own flows. v4 read the loudest 400 ms, which a game of single short sounds never fills; v5 reads the loudest 100 ms against the same -32 LUFS, and holds that at least 2 sounds of 2 kinds started, that 8 in 10 of them reached the speakers, and, when the game lists two or more sounds of its own (not on the ui bus), that one of them played. Measurements: research/open-builder/findings/audio-gate-v5-2026-10-11.md.

8.name: swap proof
8.rule: A body and a prop slot replaced by an override, as Studio does it, show the new model on screen.
8.fix: A kit test: no rules.js or config can fail it short of a load error. When it fails in a release run, fix the kit's preview page (kit/core/show.js) or the slot loader.

9.name: contact sheet and perf
9.rule: The contact sheet renders on the real graphics card and the frame rate holds (not run with --quick).
9.fix: Read the sheet folder the detail names. Lower the prop count or the look's cost in config when the frame rate is under the target.

10.name: fair play
10.rule: A player is in control at least 85% of the time alive, is back up within fair.downSeconds, and is never knocked while protected.
10.fix: Leave config/game.json → fair on. Never call p.knock(…, {force: true}) for ordinary hits, score only hits that counted (projectile.onHit and health.onDamage skip refused ones), and make bots pick foes with ctx.bots.target and fight with ctx.bots.attack.

11.name: set dressing
11.rule: The world is clean: nothing overlapping, floating or out of scale, no litter, open floor, clear spawns.
11.fix: Run node research/gf-three/tools/dressing.mjs <game>: it lists every problem with its fix in config/world.json (move, turn or remove the prop it names).

12.name: something happens
12.rule: Something happens, by the loop's own sign (kit/loops/<id> → signs.pulse). A timed round, a level run and an endless session: in three rounds with bots some score moves and builds up. Taking turns: moves are played in turn in the solo round. A match: a round of it ends with somebody ahead.
12.fix: A timed round: check the score code in rules.update against each mechanic's README, make rules.bot act (ctx.bots.target / attack, p.bot.seek), and do not make scoring depend on a score that starts at 0. Play ?bots=3&seed=1 and watch the scoreboard. A turn-taking game: the detail says what the flow counted; rules.botMove must return a move rules.move accepts.

also.what: the solo round's test player takes its own turn when a part lists one (controls().points or interactables marked turn: true), so an untimed turn shows moves; it presses nothing a part did not list

13.name: controls work
13.rule: Every control config/game.json lists does something the player sees on their own screen. On a phone (a first-person forge game), the touch buttons there at rest cover at most 5% of the screen, none sits over the middle, a readout or the menu button, each is at least 44 px across, every action is under a thumb when it applies, and How to play keeps what each control does on the screen.
13.fix: Make the control work in rules.js (for a shot: prj.fire(p) or prj.stream(p, on) with no direction lands on the crosshair). If it cannot work, take it out of config/game.json → controls so the HUD stops promising it. A phone's buttons are the kit's, laid out from config/game.json → forge.feel.touch (size, fire, gap, edge, lift, always): keep the kit's values, never hide or cover its touch layer, take a control the game does not need out of controls, and keep a touch name in controls.more to a word or two ("Load button").

also.what: when no mechanic exposes anything to walk to, a press of interact counts when it reached the flow (a move played, or refused with a reason on screen: signs.pressed), never because the turn clock ran

point and click: when a part lists what may be clicked now (window.__game.controls().points, CSS pixels, on the player's turn), primary and secondary are judged by moving the real mouse to a listed point and clicking; the point must be taken and the shared state must change. An interactable may carry its own verb

14.name: looks honoured
14.rule: A character or prop the spec asks to be generated or made from a reference is not still a stand-in, and two roles described differently never share one body file.
14.fix: Wait for the worker's generation (game/generated.json says how far it is). Give a role that is not generated its own body from library/bodies.json. Do not call Meshy or draw a stand-in in code.

15.name: the loop is alive
15.rule: Each mechanic in the spec does its job in a real round, and the thing to defend is readable on screen at round start with its health on the HUD. In a first-person wave game (forge), a new player who stands and fights is not felled by the first wave, and enemies fall to the starting weapon.
15.fix: The detail names the mechanic and the sign that was missing. Wire that mechanic's callbacks in rules.js as its README shows. A waves target is a zone name from config/world.json → zones, never a prop's name; stand the thing to defend in the centre zone. A first wave that fells the player: make forge.waves[0] smaller, slower to rise or fewer at once (enemies, delay, spawnEvery, maxAlive, attackers) and ramp the later waves; never answer it with one-hit kills (check 16).

also.what: a flow that keeps state of its own (turns, match) is sampled and judged by its own manifest's signs, like a mechanic: the turn passes and a move is played; the next round of a match starts

16.name: hits read
16.rule: A hit that does not kill changes the enemy on the player's own screen, and a basic enemy takes 2 to 4 hits.
16.fix: Keep the projectile's damage (a stream's streamDamage) below waves hp. If shots do not land, fix the aim, the range or the firing in rules.js. Set waves oneHitKills only when the spec asks for it.

17.name: the world is complete
17.rule: The play area matches the spec's size class, an indoor world is closed with real doorways, and enemies come in through doors or gates.
17.fix: Run node research/gf-three/tools/world.mjs <game>. Do not remove walls, the ceiling, doors or the outside; to re-lay the world from its template run upgrade.mjs <game> --world.

18.name: sounds play
18.rule: One sound list: every listed file is there, every audio file is played by a sound, and every id the game's code plays is listed.
18.fix: Put every sound in assets.json → sounds → sounds (never beside version), list each id rules.js plays, and remove or use any file in assets/audio/ that no sound plays.

19.name: bodies hold their shape
19.rule: Every character body keeps its face, body, arms, hands, legs and feet through every clip.
19.fix: Use another body from library/bodies.json for the role the detail names, or let the worker regenerate it. A build agent does not repair a rig by hand.

20.name: the menu works
20.rule: The game opens on the kit's home menu, Esc pauses, and How to play says the goal.
20.fix: Do not build a start screen or a pause menu, and never click, skip, hide or cover the kit's. Say the goal in one short line (at least 6 characters) in config/game.json → text.goal.

21.name: the HUD shows your state
21.rule: The kit's player card shows the player's health, knocked-down state and each mechanic's meter, with the goal line under the clock.
21.fix: Do not hide #gf-hud or draw your own health bar. Add the game's own meters with ctx.ui.meter and change the goal line with ctx.ui.goal(text), never an empty or one-word line.

22.name: the wallet in the menu
22.rule: The home menu offers Connect wallet and a worn item shows on the player.
22.fix: Do not hide #gf-wallet or recolour the local player for everyone. Read a player's look per player: ctx.assets.value(slotId, fallback, { player: p }).
22.note: A kit test in practice (the only way a game fails it is by sabotaging the kit's own page). Moved to the release run on 2026-10-11 (the creator's question 18, on the parent's recommendation): a build's verify neither runs nor requires it; verify --release and regress.mjs --corpus do.

23.name: looks like the references
23.rule: The game's own screen matches the creator's reference pictures on camera, palette, light, shapes, proportions and vibe.
23.fix: The detail names what to change. Move config/look.json values and slots toward the pictures (the preset id stays), then re-run --check 23.

24.name: plays inside a post
24.rule: Framed in a post that refuses the pointer lock, the camera stays the game's own, the full-screen button works, and in full screen a drag turns the camera and W moves.
24.fix: Never call requestPointerLock, hide #gf-fullscreen or swap the camera in rules.js.
24.note: A kit test in practice (the only way a game fails it is by sabotaging the kit's own page). Moved to the release run on 2026-10-11 (the creator's question 18, on the parent's recommendation): a build's verify neither runs nor requires it; verify --release and regress.mjs --corpus do.

also.what: in full screen W moves the player's mark when a part owns player.control and reports one

25.name: playing with friends
25.rule: Through the friends page two players name themselves, share one waiting room, play a round with no bots, and the results card shows each player the score the game counted for them.
25.fix: Never add players in rules.js (ctx.players.add) and keep rules.bot for playing alone. The results card shows p.score from the host's copy, so count each player's score in p.score on the host.

26.name: the world persists
26.rule: What a player builds is still there after everyone leaves and comes back.
26.fix: Change the world only through the build mechanic's calls, so the play host saves it; never keep world state in rules.js variables.

27.name: the host leaves and the world is kept
27.rule: When the host leaves, another player takes the world over and nothing is lost.
27.fix: Keep nothing a world needs on one player's copy: shared state goes through the kit's world store.

28.name: the spawn square holds
28.rule: Nobody can build over or dig out the place new players arrive.
28.fix: Leave the spawn protection in config on; do not place or remove blocks in the spawn square from rules.js.

29.name: sign words are filtered
29.rule: Text players write on signs and as names goes through the kit's word filter.
29.fix: Show player text only through the kit's sign and name calls, never straight into the page.

30.name: phones
30.rule: The world plays on a phone: touch controls move, look, place and break.
30.fix: Do not add key-only actions in rules.js; give each action a control in config/game.json → controls so the kit draws its touch button.

31.name: sharp on every screen
31.rule: The game draws at the screen's own pixel density on a phone, a laptop and a large display.
31.fix: A kit test: do not resize the renderer or add a canvas in rules.js. When it fails in a release run, fix kit/core/boot.js.

32.name: no WebGPU: the open-in-your-browser screen
32.rule: On a browser with no WebGPU the game shows the kit's "open in your browser" screen, never a blank canvas.
32.fix: Do not replace or hide the forge or vista boot's fallback screen (a vista game: never load gf/vista/core yourself; the boot loads it once WebGPU is there).

33.name: a lost GPU device is recovered
33.rule: When the graphics device is lost the game comes back without a reload.
33.fix: A kit test of the forge host: keep no GPU objects in rules.js.

34.name: watch then play
34.rule: A round that goes live can be watched by a viewer, who then joins.
34.fix: A kit test: do not add players in rules.js, and do not throw on a viewer's copy. When it fails in a release run, fix the kit's watch path (gf/mp).

35.name: the game's own tests
35.rule: Every test in the game's tests/ folder passes: each is one of this game's own promises (its loop, its scoring, a mechanic as this game has it, its hook, an accept item) as a play script with expect steps.
35.fix: The detail names the test, the promise's words and the expect that did not hold. Fix the game so the promise holds (rules.js, config/game.json), or, when the promise itself changed, the test with it; then re-run --check 35 (a few seconds).

36.name: the sea is drawn and moving
36.rule: Looking out to sea from the start place, the water under the horizon is drawn (not flat) and moves from frame to frame while the player stands still.
36.fix: Do not cover the view with your own HUD, change the camera or stop the core's frame in rules.js; keep config/look.json's sea state one of calm, breezy, choppy or storm.

37.name: the look is the config's
37.rule: The core draws the look config/look.json names (preset, hour, sea state, exposure, clouds), and a value Studio changes there reaches the core.
37.fix: Set the look in config/look.json, never with ctx.vista.look.set in rules.js at boot; a rule that changes the light during play (a day passing) starts from the config's values.

brief.how: A rule line is any line that is not blank, a heading, inside a code fence, or only a {{PLACEHOLDER}}. `hash` is the first 12 hex characters of the sha256 of the trimmed line; `starts` is for the reader only.

budget.why: 21 invariant lines on 2026-10-10, plus a margin of 2 (unchanged by M2-F: the cuts were sentences inside lines, and the one line that left was a part line). A new rule goes in the part it concerns; a new invariant line needs an older one to move out, or this number raised on purpose.
